title: Full CPU utilization: correct multi-threading + multi-replica campaigns
description: Two complementary parallelism layers for M-class CPUs: (a) intra-sim OpenMP (correctness prerequisites live in epic 6wo: 3zk neighbor merge bug P1, 6wo.4 epot mismatch, 6wo.3 natom guard); (b) inter-sim: the historical workflow ran many replicas for statistics — a campaign runner that fans N independent simulations across all cores is the biggest guaranteed win (embarrassingly parallel, zero contention). Needs deterministic seeding first (kps.f currently seeds from wall-clock seconds — memory: fortran-cluster-md-kps-f-kpsinit-0-seeds).

title: gfortran-native baseline: all targets build and run on Apple Silicon
description: Make gfortran (Homebrew, /opt/homebrew/bin) the DEFAULT toolchain so every target builds out of the box on M3 Pro / M1 Max — no ifort anywhere on these machines. Today only apple-silent/apple-frenkel build (via target-specific overrides); the other 10 main targets and ~30 helper targets still default to ifort and have never been compiled with gfortran. Also establishes the repo's first automated smoke-run gate, which every later epic uses as its regression check.

title: neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f: parallel neighbor list loses most neighbors under OMP_NUM_THREADS>1 (private local_counts/local_neighbors never merged across threads in SINGLE section)
description:
Reproduced with both the pre-9km and post-9km for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f (i.e. this
bug is entirely in neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f, unrelated to the force-loop file).

neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f's subroutine neighbor(step): local_neighbors(:,:) and
local_counts(:) are declared PRIVATE on the outer !$OMP PARALLEL construct, so
each thread gets its OWN copy, populated only for the atoms i it was assigned
by the DYNAMIC(32) schedule of the inner !$OMP DO. The merge step
(!$OMP SINGLE ... do i=1,natom ... local_counts(i) ...) then runs on exactly
ONE thread, reading ITS OWN private local_counts/local_neighbors — which only
has real data for the ~1/nthreads share of atoms that thread itself computed;
all other atoms' neighbor data (computed by the other threads) is silently
dropped (their private copies go out of scope, never merged into a shared
structure).

Effect: with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 the neighbor list is correct (single thread ==
single private copy == everything). With OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, atnlist ends up
with roughly 1/4 of the true neighbor count and is effectively wrong physics
for any run with >1 threads.

Repro: build apple-silent, run sample.3d (or any 3d file) with
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 vs OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and compare the neighbor-count column
in the "Step N: Updating neighborlist" screen output — count is stable (~194
for the shipped sample.3d) at 1 thread, and drops to a small, run-to-run
varying number (~45-90) at 4 threads.

Fix direction: merge each thread's local_neighbors/local_counts into the
shared atnlist inside the parallel region (e.g. an OMP CRITICAL/ORDERED
append per thread, or a two-pass count-then-fill using thread-local prefix
offsets) instead of relying on one thread's private arrays after the DO loop
ends.

title: Follow-ups epic: omp physics, build hygiene, re-parallelization
description: Wrapper epic for /goal run 2026-08-24: drains the four standalone follow-up beads discovered during epic 6x1 and bead b3v: 8ok (omp force physics divergence, P2), c2t (missing dep rules), 4bk (toolchain object separation), 9km (re-parallelize force loop, blocked on 8ok). Verification gates: make -n for ifort targets; real gfortran builds for apple targets (gfortran at /opt/homebrew/bin); 8ok/9km additionally require runtime energy comparison on sample.3d.

title: De-bloat repo per ponytail audit (~-2200 lines)
description: Ponytail repo-wide audit (2026-08-24) found ~2200 deletable lines: 17 source files unreferenced by any Makefile target, dead gpu variant, duplicated silent neighbor module, 122-line env script replaceable by one export, backup clutter git already covers, dead Makefile rules, oversized perf script. Design: pure deletion/shrink epic, no behavior change to any built target. Verification baseline for every task: 'make -n' succeeds for all main targets (silent, nuc, frenkel, apple-silent, mav) and grep shows no dangling references to removed files.

title: Harden omp neighbor builder: cap-overrun read, invalid SIMD, serial parity (dmmav, skin check)
description: Three pre-existing defects in cluster/neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f found in 3zk review, one pass fixes all: (1) P2 cap overrun — write side guards max_neighbors_per_atom=200 (line ~107) but merge read 'do j=1,local_counts(i)' (line ~123) iterates the UNCAPPED count: >200 neighbors reads past the atom's column into the next atom's slots (silently wrong indices; heap over-read for i=natom). Reachable: 5000 atoms in 8nm box hits 256-275. Fix: cap the merge loop AND add fatal stop on overflow like serial neighbor-pbc-mav.f list-full check. (2) !$OMP SIMD on the inner loop (line ~93) has loop-carried dependence via local_counts(i) increment — technically UB; remove directive. (3) Serial parity: omp version never assigns dmmav (prints 0.0) and lacks serial's skin-exceeded fatal check + adaptive atrskin update — port that logic from neighbor-pbc-mav.f. Done: dense 5000-atom/8nm run at 1 and 4 threads exits with clean physics or clean fatal (never silent corruption); dmmav printed nonzero matching serial semantics; 200-step sample byte-identity at 1 thread preserved.

title: Options catalog: kit modules, make targets, .3d field reference
description: Reverse-engineer and document every user-facing choice: 1) make targets (12 main) with their module composition (thermostat scalev/scalev-m/scalev-nh-m=Nose-Hoover, BC pbc vs walls, integrator, force variant, writers) — source: Makefile OBJ lists + cluster/README (German, translate essentials) + docs/CODE_MAP.md. 2) .3d input format: every fixed-column field read-3d.f parses (line, columns, type, meaning, valid range where known — cite read-3d.f line numbers). 3) Machine-readable mirror scripts/options.json (targets, their traits; .3d fields with column specs) — the CLI's data source. Done: docs/OPTIONS.md + scripts/options.json committed; json round-trips through python -m json.tool; every main make target appears; .3d reference covers all fields read by read-3d.f.

title: Multi-thread statistical validation after omp fixes
description: Gate for trusting OMP_NUM_THREADS>1 end-to-end. Preconditions (wired as deps): 3zk neighbor merge fix, 6wo.4 epot mismatch resolution. Method: fixed-seed 200-step run 1 vs 4 threads byte-comparison of energies (expect near-identity per 9km review); plus ensemble check — 16 replicas single-thread vs 16 replicas 4-thread (different seeds), compare mean/std of final epot/T within statistical error. Deliverable: results in bead notes + PERFORMANCE.md section 'multi-thread validated: yes/no + caveats'. Done: verdict recorded; smoke.sh extended with a 2-thread sanity case if validation passes.

title: Campaign runner: N replicas across all cores
description: Deliverable: scripts/campaign.py (python3 stdlib only). Args: binary path, input .3d, -n replicas, --jobs (default: performance-core count via sysctl hw.perflevel0.logicalcpu), --seed-base. Each replica: own output dir runs/<name>/rep-NNN/, CLUSTER_SEED=seed-base+i, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 per replica (replicas saturate cores; no nested threading), manifest.json recording seeds/exit codes/durations. Failures reported, non-zero exit if any replica fails. Done: 8-replica run of clu-silent-omp on sample-derived input completes using ~8 cores (verify wall time ~1/8 of serial-sum), outputs + manifest present.

title: Deterministic seed control via CLUSTER_SEED env
description: Input: kps.f kpsInit(0) seeds from wall-clock hh:mm:ss (main.f:41) — runs only reproducible within the same second. Fix (minimal, no .3d format change): in main.f before kpsInit, GET_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE('CLUSTER_SEED'); if set and numeric, call kpsInit with that seed (kpsInit(1) path uses fixed 65539 — extend kpsInit to accept an explicit seed value cleanly, keeping 0=wall-clock and 1=legacy-fixed behaviors intact). Done: two runs with CLUSTER_SEED=12345 byte-identical output; unset reproduces old behavior; smoke.sh still passes.

title: Smoke-run harness: one command builds+runs every main target
description: Deliverable: cluster/smoke.sh (bash 3.2 safe). For each main sim target: build, generate tiny input (copy sample.3d, sed steps=50 screen=10, rndctrl '-'), run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, assert exit 0 and at least one energy line present and finite (no NaN/***). Targets needing different inputs (diffusion uses init-center; rst multi-restart) get minimal special-casing or documented skip. Cleanup temp dirs, make clean at end. Done: ./smoke.sh exits 0 on M3 Pro, prints PASS/SKIP table; becomes the standard regression gate referenced by later beads.

title: All helper targets build with gfortran; BINDIR override
description: Input: ~30 helper targets install to $(HOME)/bin via bdir. Steps: 1) introduce BINDIR?=$(HOME)/bin, replace hardcoded $(HOME)/bin in recipes and bdir. 2) Build every helper target with BINDIR=./bin-test (never touch real $HOME/bin during verification), gfortran default from previous task. Fix legacy compile errors per-file, minimal edits. 3) rm -rf ./bin-test after. Done: every helper target links; git diff shows Makefile BINDIR change + only necessary source fixes.

title: Flip default toolchain to gfortran; all 12 main targets build
description: Input: cluster/Makefile (FF=ifort default, apple-* targets override to gfortran). Steps: 1) FF=gfortran, FLAGS=-O3 -std=legacy -ffixed-line-length-132 (plus -fopenmp only where needed), CPPFLAG=-cpp as defaults; keep ifort lines as comments for reference; collapse now-redundant apple-* target-specific overrides where they merely restate the default (APPLE_FLAGS may keep -march=native -ffast-math etc. as the optimized variant). Toolchain stamps: default targets now stamp gfortran — update stamp logic so it still guards a future ifort use, or simplify to single-compiler if that is cleaner (note choice). 2) Build ALL 12 main targets (cluster pbc mav mul nuc silent frenkel diffusion moviefrenkel nose rst test) with gfortran; fix compile errors in sources ONLY as needed (expect legacy issues; -std=legacy handles most). Watch bead 1kl pattern: any routine with mxnlist-sized automatics may need save. 3) Record warnings count per target. Done: all 12 link on M3 Pro; make clean leaves nothing; git diff reviewed target-by-target.

title: cluster-cli: guided configure, build, run, campaign
description: Python-stdlib CLI (Homebrew python installed; no third-party deps) that carries the operator through the choices the kit encodes: thermostat (scalev/scalev-m/scalev-nh-m), boundary conditions, integrator, force variant, particle counts, steps, seed — then builds the right make target, generates a valid .3d input (fixed-column format read by read-3d.f), runs with sensible OMP settings, and organizes output dirs. Foundation is a written options catalog reverse-engineered from Makefile targets, cluster/README (German), and read-3d.f.

title: Investigate: omp vs serial force epot mismatch at step 0 WITHOUT -ffast-math
description: From 9km review: with -ffast-math disabled, for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f disagrees with serial for-a-lj-n-pbc-m.f at step 0 (epot -3.38e-4 vs -2.29e-4 — ~50% relative, NOT FP noise); with full APPLE_FLAGS (incl -ffast-math) the two are byte-identical (verified in 8ok and 9km reviews). Suspicious: real expression difference that -ffast-math happens to compile identically, or reviewer's comparator setup differed (check neighbor object used, flags per binary). Reproduce carefully with identical flag sets before concluding. HEAD and post-9km omp agree exactly — predates 9km. Done: root cause identified in bead notes; if real divergence, fix + byte-identity re-check both with and without -ffast-math.

title: stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f has same cvtnt/cvtn stack-overflow bug as -m.f (apple-frenkel latent crash)
description: stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f (used by apple-frenkel/FRENKEL/DIFFUSION/MOVIEFRENKEL targets) declares cvtnt(mxnlist),cvtn(mxnlist) (mxnlist=9e6, ~36MB each) as plain local arrays, same pattern fixed in stoddard-pbc-n-m.f by fortran-cluster-md-1kl. Under APPLE_FLAGS (-fopenmp implies -frecursive), these become ~72MB per-call stack frames, overflowing the default 8MB stack the first time stoddard() is called -> SIGILL/SIGSEGV at runtime (apple-frenkel currently still builds fine, this is a runtime-only latent bug, not caught by a build check). Fix: add 'save cvtnt,cvtii,cvtn,cvti,cvtl' (or equivalent) to stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f, same as the fix applied in stoddard-pbc-n-m.f. Verify with a short apple-frenkel run on sample.3d.
notes: Scope widened per 1kl review: stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre-mov.f:30 has the SAME unsaved cvtnt(mxnlist) pattern — fix both -fre.f and -fre-mov.f (guard order also worth checking in both). Apply same fix as 1kl commit: save statement + verify arrays rebuilt-before-read.

title: omp force routine computes different physics than serial sibling
description: Pre-existing divergence found in b3v review: cluster/for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f vs for-a-lj-n-pbc-m.f differ numerically, not just in parallelization: eps11=apeps(1)*apeps(1) vs apeps(1); eps12=apeps(1)*apeps(2) vs dsqrt(...); pair-type index ij=api(i)*10+api(j) vs api(i)+api(j); fij for 22/12 cases uses c222*eps22*12.0d0 with missing -c223 attractive term. The omp and serial binaries compute different forces/energies. Decide intended physics (serial sibling is the proven reference), align omp file to it. Done: side-by-side diff of the physics expressions shows equivalence; a short two-binary run on sample.3d produces matching energies within float tolerance.

title: Sync docs/CODE_MAP.md with epic 6x1 deletions
description: Origin's docs commits (b22d1ce) landed a CODE_MAP.md written against the pre-cleanup tree; epic fortran-cluster-md-6x1 then deleted many files it documents. Stale entries (line numbers from current main): 264 for-a-lj-n-pbc-mr.f section; 295 for-w-i9-dbl-exp.f half of a dual section; 322 neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.f section (replace with note: silent build = neighbor-pbc-mav.f compiled -fpp -DSILENT); 363 stoddard-pbc-n-org.f half; 528-545 helper table rows for makelog_1.f, ratstat-t-old.f, snipfile.f, traject.f, pos.f; 564 call-tree annotation [neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.f]; 654-661 Misc section: jan_3ds.pl5, jan_verzeichnisse.pl5, test.f, hallowelt.f, prim3.f, test1.3d. Also check for setup_apple_silicon.sh/perf_test.sh/gpu mentions elsewhere in docs/. Done: grep of docs/ for every deleted filename returns nothing; surviving dual-sections (e.g. for-w-i9-dbl) keep their live half.

title: Fix apple targets mixing compilers: objects built by ifort suffix rule, linked by gfortran
description: Pre-existing latent bug found during epic fortran-cluster-md-6x1 reviews: apple-silent/apple-frenkel link with $(APPLE_FF)=gfortran but their objects compile via the .f.o suffix rule using $(FF)=ifort with $(FLAGS). On a machine without ifort the apple targets cannot build at all; mixing ifort objects with gfortran link is broken anyway. Fix idea: apple-specific pattern rule or target-specific FF/FLAGS override (GNU make target-specific vars). Also neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.o rule uses CPPFLAG=-fpp (ifort spelling); gfortran path needs -cpp. Done: 'make apple-silent' compiles AND links with gfortran end to end on Apple Silicon.

title: Fix bigclp target linking wrong object list
description: cluster/Makefile:358 bigclp links $(BIGCL__OBJ) (stoddard.o, non-PBC) instead of $(BIGCLP_OBJ) (stoddard-pbc.o) — builds non-PBC binary under PBC name. Fix: one-word change to $(BIGCLP_OBJ). Done: bigclp recipe references BIGCLP_OBJ; 'make -n bigclp' shows stoddard-pbc.o linked.

title: Merge neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.f into neighbor-pbc-mav.f (print toggle)
description: Input: two files differing only in 2 commented-out write lines (silent has them commented). Approach: single file neighbor-pbc-mav.f keeping the write; gate it behind preprocessor: rename usage so silent builds compile with -DSILENT via gfortran/ifort -cpp (fixed-form: use #ifndef SILENT around the write+format continuation). Update Makefile: SILENT/FRENKEL/DIFFUSION/MOVIEFRENKEL/NOSE/RSTOBJ/APPLE_* obj lists swap neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.o for neighbor-pbc-mav.o with a silent-flavored rule (e.g. neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.o built from neighbor-pbc-mav.f with -cpp -DSILENT — keeps object name distinct, no target-list churn). Delete neighbor-pbc-mav-silent.f. Edge cases: continuation line of the write must be inside the same #ifndef; ifort needs -fpp not -cpp — use per-compiler flag var. Done: silent file deleted; 'make -n silent' and 'make -n nuc' exit 0; compiled silent build (gfortran path) emits no per-step neighbor line, non-silent does. Ambiguity flag: if -cpp proves awkward for .f fixed form, fallback = runtime logical 'loud' in dmmpp.inc common set by main — implementer picks whichever compiles, notes choice.

title: Delete dead gpu variant + gpu-silent target + GPU_FLAGS
description: Input: cluster/for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-gpu.f (153 lines, zero OMP/offload directives), Makefile gpu-silent target (~line 269) links $(APPLE_SILENT) not the gpu file, GPU_FLAGS (~line 222). Steps: 1) delete the .f file 2) delete gpu-silent target block 3) delete GPU_FLAGS var and its comment. Done: no 'gpu' or 'GPU' occurrence left in Makefile; 'make -n apple-silent' still exits 0.

title: Delete 17 unreferenced source files
description: Input: audit list. Delete exactly: cluster/stoddard-pbc-n-org.f, cluster/for-a-lj-n-pbc-mr.f, cluster/for-w-i9-dbl-exp.f, cluster/prim3.f, cluster/hallowelt.f, cluster/test.f, cluster/helpers/ratstat-t-old.f, cluster/helpers/rdf-org.f, cluster/helpers/mkwall.f, cluster/helpers/makelog_1.f, cluster/helpers/sizer-old.f, cluster/helpers/sizer-org.f, cluster/helpers/clustat.f, cluster/helpers/pos.f, cluster/helpers/traject.f, cluster/helpers/snipfile.f, cluster/helpers/xyzsplitter.f. Do NOT touch any other .f (kit variants stay). Edge case: 'test.f' name collides with Makefile 'test' target — that target links TSTOBJ which does not contain test.o; verified unreferenced, delete anyway. Done: files gone; grep of Makefile for each basename returns nothing (excluding false substring hits like stotest/veltest); git status shows only deletions.

title: cluster-cli: campaign subcommand + quickstart docs
description: Wrap scripts/campaign.py as 'cluster-cli campaign' (delegate, don't duplicate: -n, --jobs, --seed-base pass-through, input from 'input' subcommand or file). Write README.md Quickstart section: install prereqs (brew gcc python), three commands from clone to first completed campaign, where outputs land, how to analyze (point at helpers + campaign manifest). Done: quickstart commands executed verbatim on M3 Pro succeed; README section committed.

title: cluster-cli: build + run subcommands
description: Subcommands: 'build' — pick target interactively by traits (thermostat/BC/etc from options.json) or --target NAME, invoke make, report binary; 'run' — takes binary + .3d, creates runs/<timestamp-name>/ with copies of input, sets OMP_NUM_THREADS (flag, default 1) and CLUSTER_SEED (flag), streams output, saves log + exit status. Only EXISTING make targets — no custom OBJ synthesis (yagni). Done: cluster-cli build --target silent && cluster-cli run ... completes 50-step demo end-to-end on M3 Pro.

title: cluster-cli: input generator (interactive + flags)
description: scripts/cluster-cli (python3 stdlib, subcommand 'input'): interactive prompts (with defaults from sample.3d) or pure flags for natom per species, temperature, steps, output intervals, box size, seed, rndctrl; writes fixed-column .3d validated against options.json column specs. Refuses out-of-range (natom>mxa=6000 etc). Done: generated file parses — 50-step run via clu-silent-omp exits 0; unit self-check (python -m doctest or assert block) passes.

title: Metal GPU feasibility study + go/no-go decision
description: Study only — no port. Questions: 1) technical path: Metal compute kernel for the LJ force loop behind a C shim (ISO_C_BINDING) — sketch call graph, data movement per step (positions in, forces out, natom<=6000 doubles — note Metal prefers float; precision implications for energy conservation). 2) Expected gain: measure current force-loop share of step time (Instruments or timers) at natom 1000/5000; estimate kernel+dispatch cost from Apple docs/microbench of a trivial Metal compute dispatch (~10-50us); compute break-even natom. 3) Alternative uses of effort: campaign mode already saturates CPU. Deliverable: docs/GPU_FEASIBILITY.md with numbers + recommendation; then bd human fortran-cluster-md-r7a asking operator for go/no-go. Done: doc committed, human flag raised, NO implementation started.

title: Benchmark + thread-guidance doc for M3 Pro / M1 Max
description: Extend cluster/perf_test.sh or new scripts/bench.sh: dilute (sample.3d natom=1000) and dense (natom=5000, small box — reuse 9km review recipe) configs; 1/2/4/8 threads; also one campaign-mode datapoint (8 replicas x 1 thread vs 1 replica x 8 threads on equal total work). Output: docs/PERFORMANCE.md with measured table from the machine it ran on + recommendation (small systems: campaign mode; large: OMP threads; numbers for the 6wo.3 natom guard threshold). Done: doc committed with real numbers, script re-runnable.

title: GPU feasibility spike (Metal) — study only, no port
description: Apple Silicon has no CUDA and gfortran's OpenMP offload cannot target Metal — the only GPU path is a Metal compute kernel behind a C shim called from Fortran (force loop). For natom 1000-6000 the kernel may not amortize dispatch overhead vs 6-8 performance cores. One study bead: measure, estimate, recommend go/no-go via bd human. The port itself is NOT planned until the human approves — speculative GPU work would be pure YAGNI.

title: omp force loop: natom guard + reuse atnidx CSR index
description: From 9km review. (1) Parallel force loop is 4.5x SLOWER at natom=1000 (sample.3d) but 1.58x faster at natom=5000 dense — add runtime guard (if natom below threshold, run serial branch; threshold ~2000-3000, calibrate). (2) Simplification: pass-1 segment walk is redundant — every neighbor builder already maintains atnidx CSR index; istart(i)=atnidx(i)+1, iend(i)=atnidx(i+1)-1 deletes the serial walk. Done: guard + CSR swap in for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f; byte-identity at 1 thread on 200-step fixed-seed run; timing shows no regression at 5000 atoms.

title: Investigate: stoddard neighbor walk truncates at first non-type-1 neighbor
description: Found in 1kl review, pre-existing: cluster/stoddard-pbc-n-m.f — 'if (api(j).ne.1) goto 110' where label 110 is the LOOP EXIT, so the walk stops at the first non-type-1 neighbor instead of skipping it. In mixed-species runs (sample.3d has Ar+He) cluster detection may silently ignore neighbors after the first He. Possibly intentional (cluster analysis over species 1 only?) — check siblings stoddard-pbc-n.f / -fre.f for same pattern and thesis context in docs. Deliverable: analysis note in bead + fix if clearly a bug; if intent ambiguous, flag with bd human for operator physics decision. Done: bead notes state verdict with code evidence; any fix keeps 200-step energies identical for pure-species runs.

title: Audit + fix stale .inc dep lists across all existing Makefile rules

Known: read-3d.o omits atomc.inc (missed rebuild — real bug); wrt-rst.o lists atomp.inc but source includes atomc.inc (check both directions); chk-nucleation.o lists atomc.inc+timep.inc source doesn't include (spurious rebuilds only). Done: script comparison of each rule's .inc list vs source includes shows zero mismatches; make -n silent/nuc/frenkel/mav/apple-silent/cluster/pbc exit 0.

Options: per-toolchain obj subdir, or .o suffix per toolchain, or make benchmark insert make clean between the two. Done: make benchmark produces both binaries correctly from scratch; sequential apple-silent then silent build does not reuse stale objects (verify via file timestamps or nm).
notes: Additional scope from 8ok review: make clean only rm -f *.o — linked binaries (clu-silent-omp, clu-fre-omp, cluster, clu-*) survive; extend clean to remove them.

title: Re-parallelize omp force loop + cleanup orphans
description: b3v removed invalid OMP directives from the packed-neighbor-list force loop in for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f, leaving it serial (directives were unbuildable under gfortran and semantically broken: shared cursor k, DO WHILE not worksharing-able). To regain parallel speedup: restructure traversal so iterations are independent (e.g. per-atom loop over a CSR-style index array built by neighbor routine) then reapply OMP DO with reduction on esum and atomic/reduction on fsum arrays. Also cleanup: 6 orphaned !$OMP ATOMIC in the now-serial loop (pure overhead), unused variable tid (line ~20). Depends on physics fix bead — align expressions first, then parallelize. Done: apple-silent builds, multi-thread run on sample.3d matches single-thread energies, measurable speedup over serial force loop.

title: Add missing Makefile dep rules for omp + m-variant objects
description: These objects build only via implicit .f.o fallback with no .inc dependency tracking (stale-header rebuilds go unnoticed): for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.o, int-verlet-mav-omp.o, neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.o, stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.o, stopdead-m.o, wrt-xyz-m-vmd.o. Also for-a-dummy.o rule exists but no OBJ list references it — decide keep (kit stub) or drop. Done: each listed .o has explicit rule with correct .inc deps mirroring its siblings; make -n silent/nuc/frenkel/apple-silent exit 0.

description: Steps: 1) delete dependency rules for kit parts no OBJ list links: for-a-lj1..4, int-euler1, int-euler2, int-gear3, int-gear4, int-gear5, int-verlet (plain), for-w-i12, for-w-iX, for-w-i9g, for-w-i9-dbl, for-w-lj, stoddard-pbcsw-n, for-a-lj-n-pbcsw, neighbor-pbcsw-mav (keep the .f files — reference kit).
